O blessed that robber, who suddenly earned such holiness, and at the very point of death passed over to the light. And those two robbers showed, the one your image, the other ours. You killed the Lord, and you rejoice: you killed indeed, and yet you did not kill; you killed in will, but you did not kill in truth, because Christ remains forever. The body lay indeed in the tomb, but Christ reigned in heaven. For it could not enclose .......... .............. is not enclosed in the tomb with the body, much more could the divinity not be enclosed. So Christ lives forever; as the holy angel Gabriel also said to glorious Mary: He will reign in the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end (Luke 1); and in the seventy-first psalm it is said of him: In his days righteousness will arise, and abundance of peace. When he said: Whoever strikes you on the right cheek, offer him the other also; and to him who wishes to go to law with you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well. What is more just, what more useful, than to overcome the impatient by patience, and to be crushed by losses rather than to sin by gaining! For these are the precepts of justice of the Lord Saviour set out in the holy Gospel. And not to be long in saying it all, after some words there follows: and abundance of peace, until the moon is taken away (Psalm 71). Abundance of peace, because he himself is the purest fountain of peace, in which there are no turbulent strifes, no bitterness of malice, but all fullness of sweetness and all tranquillity of goodness. Of him the prophet David himself said in another place: Taste and see that the Lord is sweet. Blessed is the man who hopes in him (Psalm 33); because the Lord said: My peace I give you, my peace I leave you. For by this all men will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another (John 14). And again he said: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God. Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 5). And abundance, he says, ............ ................................. ................. ..... But afterwards it is lifted up and raised, when with the Lord's help it is led to the heavenly kingdoms. There follows in the psalm: And he shall have dominion from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the world (Psalm 71): that is, through all nations and through the whole world, wherever the circuit of Ocean, spread far and wide, runs, and encloses the bounds of all lands. There follows: Before him the Ethiopians will fall down, and his enemies will lick the earth (ibid.). Those Ethiopians are the spirits of darkness, who before the Lord, that is, at his coming, troubled ........... ................. ................. ................. but they are said to lick the earth; how do these too .. .. and lick the earth? That is, [because] they love the earthly letter and carnal cunning, but do not seek spiritual grace? There follows in the psalm: The kings of the earth and the islands offer gifts. The kings of the Arabs and of Saba bring presents (ibid.). East and West, then; and this was shown again in the holy Gospel, when the magi came bearing gifts, gold, frankincense, myrrh: offering gold as precious faith to a king; sweet frankincense, a sacrifice of praise, as to God; myrrh as a sign and service of burial. Again, gold to the king, frankincense to the priest, myrrh to the sacrifice: because Christ is Lord and king, and priest, and sacrifice. That he is king, he himself says: But I have been set up as king by him (Psalm 2); that he is priest: You, says the Father to him, are a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek (Psalm 9). The apostle Paul calls [him] a sacrifice, who offered himself as an offering and victim to God for an odour of good sweetness (Ephesians 5). Gold, frankincense and myrrh. The king seeks gold, that is, chosen hearts; God [seeks] frankincense, chaste and good prayers, for an odour of good fragrance; myrrh for the burial of his saints. So from every side the peoples brought gifts to Christ. There follows in the psalm: And all the kings of the earth shall worship him; all nations shall serve him (Psalm 71): which we see fulfilled, because everywhere the name of the Lord Christ is worshipped by all kings, at least the Christian ones, and by all nations. But even if there are some kings or some nations who will not worship, as you Jews too [will not], the eternal prison awaits, the judgement of God awaits: God, says the prophet, our God will come manifest, and will not delay (Psalm 49); he who came hidden in humility will come manifest in power. Then all flesh will see him, that is, every human being, because we shall all stand before the judgement seat of Christ, so that each may receive the things of the body, according to what he has done, whether good or evil (Romans 14); for in that very psalm, at its head, he says: O God, give your judgement to the king, and your justice to the king's son (Psalm 71); because the Lord Christ himself is king and son of the king; and at the conclusion of the psalm he says: The whole earth shall be filled with his glory: so be it, so be it (ibid.). And we, agreeing with the holy prophet with the Lord's voice, say: Amen, amen, that is, truly, faithfully. This repetition of the word contains in itself a confirmation of the truth. Thanks be to God. So the Jews are plainly refuted: with God's help let us speak thus against them, not out of eagerness to harm, so as to destroy them once defeated, far be it from us; a spiritual battle is waged for the salvation of men: let our weapons not be carnal, but mighty from God. And so we desire to save them and to turn [them] under [the rule] of our king Christ. Let us not, then, seek strife, since we seek the truth; we serve as soldiers under a peaceable king, and we follow the camp of peace. And therefore, as I said, we wish to lead them from the stormy waves of error to the harbour of salvation, and through the court of truth to bring them into the royal house of our Lord, so that from enemies they may become friends, and from antichrists Christians. Let them see the spiritual pasture; let them see, if they deserve it, the heavenly banquet; let them see the Lord's table, and sing with us, with David the most holy prophet, saying: The Lord feeds me, and I shall lack nothing; in a place of pasture there he has set me (Psalm 22); and again: How lovely are your tabernacles, Lord of hosts! My soul longs and faints for the courts of the Lord (Psalm 83). But the impious Jews resist this persuasion, and would rather die than be overcome, saying: We worship one God, as it is written in the books of Moses: You shall have no other gods besides me, and you shall worship the Lord your God and serve him alone; and: Hear, O Israel, the Lord your God is one Lord (Deuteronomy 6). This precept, they cry, was given to the fathers, and it is right and fitting that we keep it. To them we say: Tell us then why your fathers, abandoning this one God, turned to idols? And they made a calf in Horeb, and worshipped a carved image, and exchanged their glory for the likeness of a calf that eats hay (Psalm 105); and they served the host of heaven? They add: That is their affair; we do not know. To them we say: Hear then, and learn: this admonition was given by God for this reason, that he might turn [them] to himself ...... From this they took to themselves groves (4 Kings 21), from this unlawful sacrifices, from this many gods, from this false figments and empty idols. Therefore the Lord, wishing, as we said, to turn them from such great errors to the worship of his majesty, frequently thundered in sacred speech, saying: You shall have no other gods besides me, and you shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone; and: Hear, O Israel, the Lord your God is one Lord (Deuteronomy 6). For, that you may know for certain what the Christian faith is, we believe, worship and venerate that one Lord, invisible, incorporeal, immortal, without beginning and without end ....... you may deserve, we are zealous in preaching the truth; and therefore after what we have said we take up further divine testimonies, to prove that Christ is God and the Son of God, as we have already set out in some [places]. God the almighty Father says to Moses in Deuteronomy (chapter 18) concerning Christ his Son: I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brothers like you; and I will put his word in his mouth, and he will speak to them whatever I tell him. And if anyone does not hear your prophet, I will avenge [it]. And again we read in Kingdoms: I will raise up for myself a faithful priest, who will do according to all that is in my heart (1 Kings 2); and in the Gospel the Father himself says: This is my most beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear him (Matthew 17) .. ..... he says; and him ..... he says, hear him ........... the word to himself, and fitting to them, he is shown to be, and a prophet, who is Christ the Lord, the Son of God; he is called the Prophet of the Father; but he is Lord of the Father's prophets; Prophet by right, as the preacher of his author, while himself bestowing the grace of prophecy on the others. For just as he is called Prophet, he is also called Angel by the Father, as it is written: Behold, I send my Angel before your face, who will prepare your way; heed him, and obey him, and do not be disobedient to him: for he will not fail you; for my name is in him (Exodus 23); whence the Lord Christ himself also said in the holy Gospel: I have come in the name of my Father, and you have not received me; when another comes in his own name, him you will accept (John 5); and David said: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord (Psalm 117). But it is said .. and the writings of the other prophets, and from there let us search out the rule of truth, and repeat what we have already put forward. Blessed Moses, enlightened by the Holy Spirit, said in the book of Genesis (chapter 1): In the beginning God made heaven and earth. Notice at once that he began from the beginning and named the beginning, by which we understand that Christ is called the beginning, in whom God the Father made heaven and earth; he made heavenly and earthly things alike in Christ, that is, in his power, who served the command of the one ordering; in him he made [them]; whatever was commanded, he fulfilled; because of the Father it is written: He spoke, and they were made; he commanded, and all things were created (Psalm 32); therefore in the beginning, that is ... ........ God made heaven and earth; he created me as the beginning of his ways for his works. Before the ages he established me; and again, in the person of wisdom, Christ himself says of himself through the prophet: I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, firstborn before every creature (Ecclesiasticus 24). Therefore in this Son and through him, as has often been said, God the almighty Father made all things, as again he said in the psalm: At the head of the book it is written of me (Psalm 39). But, says the Jew, he who spoke is the same who made. To him we say: And what need was there for him to speak? If there was no other to hear and do, was he saying to himself, Let it be? But again the Jew says: He spoke to the angels; to whom we say: But the angels did not make [it], but he has, and God made ..... ........ the Jew; and he says: How ......... that God has a son ........ the Jew invisible, and in ..... to whom again ..... we answer as the Lord did: Is it not said in your law: I said, You are gods, and dearest sons of the Most High? If he called those gods and sons of the Most High to whom the word of God came, and Scripture cannot be broken, you are angry with me, says the Lord, because I said, I am the Son of God? If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me; but if I do, even if you will not believe me, believe the works (John 10). Then we say: How does that seem to the Jews which David says, without doubt in the person of Christ: The Lord said to me: You are my Son; today I have begotten you? And again, in the person of the Father, the most holy prophet David himself says to the Son: With you is the beginning in the day of your power, in the splendours of the saints; from the womb before the morning star I begot you (Psalm 109). Whom he begot ..... he says, so do you believe that ..... we answer, thus the Prophet ..... and we so believe [that he] begot ..... but that ..... ............... of holy divine gen. ..... as for God to beget: the Lord begot the Lord, light light, splendour splendour, the mighty the mighty, king king, one one, only only, eternal eternal, power power, creator creator. These things we have already said, and we say them as far as we are able. For the rest, that is inexplicable and unspeakable, that he is Father and Son; the Son of the Father, the Word of the Father, the power and wisdom of the Father, in whom and through whom the Father made all things. Understand this Word as the Son of God, whom he sent for the salvation of the world, as the prophet said: He sent his Word, and healed them (Psalm 106). Therefore he is called Son of God who is the Word of the Father, not as you, with a fleshly and culpable mind, understand us to say that God begot carnally. For hear Isaiah (chapter 53), the holy prophet, saying of Christ: But who shall declare his generation? Can it be said or explained how the Father begot the Son, how God brought forth the Word? ..... I want to understand how you believe these things about Christ; to whom we say: Hear: it is written, the Father saying: With you is the beginning in the day of your power, in the splendours of the saints; from the womb before the morning star I begot you (Psalm 109); he who says 'you' shows that there is another, that is, his Son, second from him, to whom he says 'you': he who says 'you' declares that there are two persons, both his who speaks and his to whom he speaks. From the womb, he says, before the morning star I begot you. By 'womb' here I understand the depth of majesty, the unspeakable fullness and profound mystery, the incomprehensible wisdom of God: before the morning star I begot you; either before the adornment of the heaven, or before the beginning of the Holy Spirit, because the Holy Spirit himself is called the morning star, who pours the light of truth and good faith into human minds, and who through the prophets very often announced, like a morning star, the coming of Christ the eternal sun. For this Lord Christ, the Son of God, was seen by many saints even before, and is known to have appeared earlier: to Abraham, and Jacob, and Moses, and to the children of Israel in the pillar of fire and cloud, of whom God the Father had said: Behold, I send my angel before your face, who will prepare your way before you (Mark 1); and he was seen by the son of Nave, and said: I am the prince of the host of the power of the Lord (Joshua 3); he is certainly also the Son of the Father; and he is called his Angel, that is, messenger, and prophet, and priest, and servant, and advocate, and power, and wisdom, and the rest. For that he was seen by Abraham, hear Scripture (Genesis 22) saying: The angel of the Lord called Abraham from heaven, and said: Abraham, Abraham, do not stretch out your hand against the boy ..... whence in what follows you will find it written that the Lord rained fire and sulphur from the Lord upon the two cities Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19). Do you hear that the Lord rained from the Lord? Which Lord? From which Lord, if not the Son from the Father? For he himself also appeared to Jacob, and wrestled with him; whence Jacob himself says: I have seen the Lord face to face, and my soul has been saved (Genesis 32); he had certainly seen Christ, with whom he wrestled, in the form of the body which he was afterwards to take up. For of the Father it is written: Whom no man has seen, nor can see (John 1); and again: No man, says God the Father himself, can see my face and live (Exodus 33). The very Angel of the Lord, who is Christ, appeared to Moses in the bush, in fire; and he himself said: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and of Jacob; he who is first said to have appeared as the Angel of the Lord in the fire; he himself .... is then said (Exodus 3) also to have said: I am the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob .... to the son of Nave, standing on the bank of the river by Jericho, appeared ....... the Lord Christ himself, holding a sword in his hand; and when Jesus said to him: Are you our lord, or of our adversaries? the Lord said to him: I am the prince of the host of the power of the Lord (Joshua 3); this is the prince seeking the principality, and he himself is the king set up by the Father, as he himself testifies, saying: But I have been set up as king by him (Psalm 2). For also in a certain psalm David, speaking in the person of Christ himself, said: Offer to God a sacrifice of praise, and pay your vows to the Most High, and call upon me in the day of distress, and I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me (Psalm 49). In these verses he admonishes that sacrifice should be offered to God the Father, and that he himself should be called upon, so that he may help his suppliants; as if he said: Render to the Father the service of praise, and I will give you the help of a protector; honour the one who begot, and you will find me a helper. Whence he himself also said in the holy Gospel: I honour my Father, and you have dishonoured me (John 8). We Christians, therefore, believe in and confess one God the Father, and one Lord our Jesus Christ his Son, of whom both the law and the prophets spoke, and through him we pray to God the Father, and give thanks to him, because the Saviour himself so commanded us, saying, [as he did] to all who are willing to believe: This is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent (John 17). Therefore, knowing the precepts of our Saviour Christ, let us always praise the one God the Father through him, to whom be glory for ever. Amen.
